newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE sugar hit by EU tender, dull NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE sugar hit by EU tender, dull NY.

text.p: Nearby LIFFE sugar eased after a larger than expected EU tender award and a disappointing performance from New York, traders said.
By 1530 GMT August sugar was $2.50 lower at $319.40, on volume of 2,191 lots of a total 3,347.

A total of 58,700 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 41.628 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
This was heavier than expected, and put London under pressure, one trader said.
New York's trend down in early trade, with spot October breaching nearby support at 11.20 cents per lb also weighed on London, he said.
Thailand's decision to float the baht had little impact, despite Thailand's role as a sugar producer, traders said.
Thailand floated the baht on Wednesday in a bold move which jolted its stock exchange out of the doldrums and sent shock waves through Southeast Asian markets.
The baht plunged by 15-20 percent in offshore markets despite a bid to offset the blow by the central Bank of Thailand, which raised its lending rate by two percentage points to 12.5 percent.
